inputs.share_count_basis: 5,299.303m shares in issue less 27.07m treasury shares (24.44m A + 2.63m H) at 30 June 2026 per the H1 2026 interim report; no options, convertibles or other dilutive instruments (diluted EPS = basic). Held FLAT: SBC is zero and buybacks are value-neutral in this model. A further ~19m A shares (~RMB340m) were repurchased in July 2026 under the RMB600m-1,000m programme; not netted because the cash left the balance sheet after the 30 June anchor.
inputs.cash_composition: 30 June 2026, RMB m: cash and cash equivalents 13,539 + bank deposits with original maturity over three months 20,244 + time deposits (current 5,163 + non-current 16,349) + structured deposits and wealth management products at FVPL 22,981 (principal; all rated R1 low risk, CMBC Wealth Management counterparties) + other financial assets 2,730 = 81,006. Restricted cash deposits (545) and listed equity securities (470, carried in the equity bridge) excluded.
inputs.debt_composition: 30 June 2026, RMB m: bank loans and other borrowings 7,409 current + 5,728 non-current; corporate bonds 3,159 current + 9,500 non-current; lease liabilities 35 + 290; long-term payables (instalment mining rights) 172 + 1,353 = 27,645. Ties to Metrics.csv TotalDebt for H1 FY2026.
inputs.interest_income_note: FY2025 interest income was RMB1,916.6m (other income note 6). It is NOT deducted from last_fcf because under Conch's IFRS cash-flow presentation interest received (1,696m) sits in INVESTING activities, so reported OCF-less-capex already excludes it. It IS stripped from the forward EBITDA margin path: every margin below is operating EBITDA ex interest income, FVPL gains, dividend income, FX and disposal gains, because the cash pile that earns them is added to EV in the bridge.
inputs.sbc_source: Zero. No share-based payment scheme; the FY2025 cash-flow reconciliation (note 29(b)) carries no SBC add-back and the Metrics.csv StockBasedComp column is 0 in every period. SBC-zero market: house and street bases coincide.
inputs.buyback_note: FY2025 financing outflow for repurchases was nil; FY2024 RMB161m, FY2023 RMB339m, H1 2026 RMB83m. The May 2026 RMB600m-1,000m A-share programme had executed ~RMB383m by end-July 2026 (Analysis.json). Flat share count is therefore partly funded, but value-neutral either way.
inputs.fx_note: Statements and all flows in RMB (CNY); H shares quoted in HKD. CNYHKD=X 1.1721 from Yahoo Finance, 2026-10-10T03:38Z. Per-share values are computed in CNY and multiplied by 1.1721 to the HKD quote basis. Parity check is NOT available because the dual listing is an A share (600585.SS), which trades at a premium rather than at parity: 600585.SS RMB17.39 at 2026-10-09 close vs the H share at 15.99 HKD / 1.1721 = RMB13.64, a 21.5% H-share discount, within the usual A/H band for the name. Direction check: 15.99 HKD x (1/1.1721) = RMB13.64, so H-share market cap = 5,272m x 13.64 = ~RMB71.9bn.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-09T08:08:06Z regular HKEX close (Friday); valuation written Sunday 2026-10-11, no after-hours print
inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in CNY, the currency of the flows: 10-year China Government Bond ~1.8% + beta 1.2 x China equity risk premium ~6.5% = ~9.6% cost of equity, rounded to 9.5%. Conch is net cash (RMB53bn) so the pre-tax debt cost (~2-3% on RMB bonds) carries negligible weight and WACC ~ cost of equity. The 1.2 beta is the cyclical premium: cement earnings swing with fixed-asset and property investment (H1 2026 attributable profit -42.8% on revenue -10.9%). Risk is charged ONCE: the same 9.5% is used in all three scenarios; the demand downcycle, overcapacity and price war are modelled in the scenario flows and the 30/50/20 weights, not by stacking a further discount-rate premium.
inputs.lease_treatment: (A) leases as debt. Lease liabilities (RMB325m at 30 June 2026) are inside total_debt; lease rentals paid (RMB81m FY2025, in financing) are NOT deducted from the flows; EBITDA is post-IFRS-16 and D&A includes right-of-use depreciation. Leases are immaterial for a company that owns its quarries and plants.
inputs.nci_treatment: Charged once, in the bridge: non-controlling interests of RMB10,695m (30 June 2026 book) deducted as an equity_bridge item. Flows are consolidated. NCI's share of profit was -243m in FY2025 and -25m in FY2024 (loss-making minorities, e.g. West Papua Conch ramp-up), so a leakage driver inside the flows would be unstable; deducting the stock is the conservative choice.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF, 10-year explicit horizon, probability-weighted scenarios, routed via dcf-methods SKILL.md row 'operating company, non-US or cyclical' with the adaptations file (currency, leases, NCI, matching-asset rule, SBC-zero, charge-risk-once). First valuation of this ticker; no memory entry. MID-CYCLE NORMALISATION: FY0 = FY2025 revenue RMB82.5bn. FY2026 is treated as a trough year (H1 2026 revenue -10.9%, self-produced cement/clinker revenue -16.5% on volume -4% and price ~-13%; self-produced gross margin 22.5%, down 6.4pp; FY2026 volume guidance 260mt vs 265mt sold in FY2025). The base case does not extrapolate the FY2025 margin (operating EBITDA 20.9% of revenue, flattered by coal costs falling 15.7%/t faster than prices): it drops to 17.5% in FY2026, recovers to a 20% mid-cycle level by FY2030 and holds there into the terminal year. 20% is the FY2022-FY2025 range on a self-produced revenue basis (19-22%); the 28-30% EBITDA margins of 2018-2021 are not treated as recurring because national cement output has fallen from ~2.4bn t to ~1.7bn t with ~30% structural overcapacity remaining. EBITDA DEFINITION: operating EBITDA = profit from operations + D&A - (interest income + FVPL gains + dividend income + disposal gains - FX loss). FY2025: 19,240 - 2,008 = 17,232 (20.9%); FY2024: 19,376 - 1,887 = 17,489 (19.2%). Subsidy income (VAT refunds on resource-utilisation cement, RMB847m FY2025) is kept inside operating EBITDA as recurring; PP&E impairments (RMB820m FY2025) are left as an operating cost, i.e. not added back. CASH TAX 24% flat on EBIT (FY2025 effective 23.7%, cash paid 3,054m on PBT 10,775m; statutory 25% with some 15%-rate high-tech subsidiaries). WORKING CAPITAL: wc_capture -10% (receivables + inventories exceed payables + contract liabilities, so growth consumes cash and the FY2026-27 revenue decline releases it, consistent with the +2.5bn WC inflow in FY2025). CAPEX: FY2025 cash capex (PP&E 8,113 + intangibles 1,524) = 9,636m, 11.7% of revenue; management budget for 2026 RMB11,820m includes acquisitions. Base path starts at 13% of a lower FY2026 revenue (~9.7bn, H1 2026 ran at 3.3bn) and settles at 11.5% (~RMB8.7-9.5bn), slightly above D&A (~11%) to fund aggregates/concrete, overseas (Cambodia, Indonesia) and new-energy expansion. FY2022 capex (RMB26.6bn incl. 12.6bn intangibles/mining rights) is not a base. NET CASH is ~74% of the H-share market cap: the valuation is more a question of whether the market will credit the RMB81bn of deposits and R1-rated wealth-management products than of cement margins; see cash_composition. Lease and NCI treatments stated above. Terminal: cap multiple 12x owner FCF base (cyclical, structurally declining end-market), 14x bull, 10x bear; terminal growth 1.5% base (China nominal growth minus cement volume decline), 2.0% bull, 0.5% bear. SBC-zero: band_position is null, house = street.
inputs.fcf_cross_check: FY2025 component build: operating EBITDA 17,232 - D&A 8,464 = EBIT 8,768; x(1-24%) = 6,664; + D&A - capex 9,636 = 5,492; + WC release ~0.8bn = ~6.3bn vs reported FCF 6,235. FY2026 base year-1 owner FCF ~3.0bn (H1 2026 actual OCF - capex = 873m) is a trough, not a run-rate.

equity_bridge.item: Interests in associates and joint ventures at book
equity_bridge.note: 30 June 2026: associates 6,164 + JVs 2,354 (RMB m). Share of associate/JV profit (RMB650m FY2025) sits below profit from operations and is excluded from the EBITDA flows, so the asset is added at book (matching-asset rule). West China Cement (2233.HK) is the largest associate.
30 June 2026: FVPL listed equities 470 (Gansu Shangfeng, Tianshan Material) + financial assets at FVOCI 1,185. Dividend income (RMB99m FY2025) is excluded from operating EBITDA.
30 June 2026 NCI RMB10,694.9m deducted once here; flows are consolidated (see nci_treatment).

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: terminal growth of the explicit driver path (base case); neither the equity CAGR (+3.5%, held up by retained earnings on a 55% payout) nor the revenue/EPS CAGRs (-14%/-25%, inflated by the 2022 wind-down of the low-margin trading business and the cement price collapse) describes forward growth
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5-yr CAGR +3.5% vs revenue -14.1% and EPS -24.8%: divergence far beyond the 30% threshold. Book value compounds from retained profit while revenue and earnings are in a cyclical and structural downcycle; the FY2022 revenue drop (-21%) also reflects exiting most of the cement trading business, so revenue CAGRs overstate the decline in the self-produced business.
historical_growth.notes: Owner FCF equals reported FCF (OCF - capex) throughout: SBC is zero and interest received sits in investing. FCF 3-yr CAGR is undefined because FY2022 FCF was -17.5bn (capex 26.6bn incl. 12.6bn of mining rights/intangibles). FCF FY2020 24.4bn -> FY2025 6.2bn. Revenue FY2020 176.2bn -> FY2025 82.5bn; EPS 6.64 -> 1.60; attributable equity 161.7bn -> 192.4bn.

base.narrative: FY2026 trough (-9.5%: H1 -10.9%, easier H2 comps), FY2027 -3% as price competition persists, flat FY2028, then +2% nominal as aggregates, concrete, overseas and the anti-involution capacity controls offset a slowly shrinking domestic cement volume. Operating EBITDA margin troughs at 17.5% and recovers to a 20% mid-cycle level by FY2030. Capex settles at 11.5% of revenue, D&A 11%.

bull.narrative: Anti-involution capacity retirement and off-peak production discipline restore pricing from FY2027; fiscal infrastructure push ('two prioritisations', urban renewal) stabilises volumes; overseas (Cambodia, Indonesia, exports +77% H1 2026) and aggregates/concrete grow into a larger mix. Margin rebuilds to 23% (FY2022 level) as the lowest-cost producer takes share from retiring capacity and buys distressed assets cheaply.

bear.narrative: No bottom in property; national cement output keeps falling ~5-8%/yr through FY2028 and the price war continues because capacity controls are not enforced on registered-vs-actual capacity. Coal rebounds while prices stay weak, so the operating margin sinks to 15%; D&A is sticky on a shrinking revenue base and capex cannot fall below 12% because the diversification spend is what keeps the company relevant. Carbon ETS inclusion adds cost from FY2027. Owner FCF stays positive but thin (~RMB1.5-2bn), so most of the value is the balance sheet.

scenario_narratives.base: A cyclical trough in FY2026-27 inside a structurally shrinking Chinese cement market. Revenue bottoms around RMB72bn in FY2027 and grows ~2% a year thereafter as aggregates, commodity concrete, overseas plants and consumer building materials grow faster than domestic cement declines. Operating EBITDA margin (ex interest and investment income) troughs at 17.5% and normalises to 20% mid-cycle by FY2030, the FY2022-25 average on a self-produced basis, never the 28-30% of 2018-21. Capex stays modestly above D&A. Terminal value capped at 12x owner FCF. Roughly three-quarters of the per-share value is the RMB53bn net cash and investment portfolio, so the base case is a judgment about capital allocation (dividends, buybacks, counter-cyclical M&A) as much as cement economics.
scenario_narratives.bull: Policy-driven consolidation works: the MIIT 2025-26 work plan retires misaligned capacity, off-peak production holds, and the 15th Five-Year Plan infrastructure push plus urban renewal stabilise demand near 1.6bn t. Conch, as the lowest-cost producer (unit cost ~RMB165/t), regains pricing and rebuilds a 23% operating margin by FY2029 while overseas revenue compounds at 20%+ and share buybacks continue. Terminal cap 14x.
scenario_narratives.bear: The property adjustment runs for years and infrastructure stimulus fades; cement output falls toward 1.3-1.4bn t by 2028 with ~30% overcapacity unresolved. Price competition persists, coal rebounds, carbon costs rise. Margin settles at 15-15.5%, revenue shrinks to ~RMB60bn, owner FCF of ~RMB1.5-2bn a year is mostly absorbed by diversification capex. Equity value is close to the net cash plus associates; the operating business is worth little more than its terminal cap of 10x a thin FCF.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 30%: single-market (China) exposure to a demand series that has fallen for five years with no confirmed bottom, structural overcapacity near 30%, and H1 2026 showing the price war intensifying rather than easing. Bull cut to 20% because it needs several independent things to go right (capacity enforcement, property stabilisation, coal staying cheap, overseas scaling). Base 50%. Solvency risk is nil (net cash RMB53bn), which is why bear is not higher: the bear case is a thin operating business on a fortress balance sheet, not distress.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value Conch as a through-cycle owner-FCF stream plus a very large, separately itemised net cash and investment portfolio. The operating margin path is normalised to a mid-cycle level derived from the post-2021 era rather than the peak years, cyclicality is priced in the scenario flows and a 30% bear weight rather than by stacking WACC premia, and the terminal multiple is capped at 10-14x because cement is a structurally declining end-market in China. The H-share price currently sits near the bear-case value, i.e. the market is paying for the balance sheet and crediting the cement business with roughly nothing.
key_risks_to_valuation: Net cash and wealth-management products (RMB81bn gross) are ~74% of the H-share market cap; the valuation depends on this capital being returned or reinvested at a reasonable return rather than trapped in low-yield deposits or spent on marginal M&A. A 20% haircut to the cash pile is ~HK$3.6/share.

Mid-cycle margin of 20% may be too high if Chinese cement demand keeps falling toward 1.3bn t and capacity controls are not enforced; each 1pp of terminal margin is ~RMB0.75bn of EBITDA, ~HK$1/share of value.
Coal and power are 52-57% of unit cost; a coal price spike compresses margins faster than cement prices adjust (H1 2026 pattern).
Carbon ETS inclusion and dual-carbon mandates add a structural cost not separately modelled beyond the margin path.
Related-party asset roll-ups from Conch Holdings (RMB619-691m in 2026) and NCI-funded overseas JVs are capital allocation decisions outside minority control.
FX: value computed in CNY and translated at a single spot CNYHKD rate; a 5% RMB move is ~HK$1/share.
